decision.reasoning: Stability above ideology: a nuclear crisis or a Hormuz closure destroys Vision 2030 far faster than any diplomatic embarrassment, so we spend diplomatic capital, not military capital, and we keep both the American and Chinese channels warm rather than choosing. Normalization is paused, not dead — signing under Netanyahu's election clock without a Palestinian deliverable would be a legitimacy crisis with the religious establishment for a gain we can obtain later on better terms. We are loss-averse: holding production steady while advertising spare capacity reassures markets and buyers without gambling revenue or provoking OPEC+ partners.
decision.researchNote: Two-level games best explains this: the East Jerusalem condition and the religious establishment shrink the domestic win-set so narrowly that Riyadh must convert American normalization pressure into a different currency — regional crisis mediation and air-defense guarantees — rather than pay at Level II.

decision.primaryAction: Launch an emergency, high-visibility mediation push: dispatch the Secretary of State and the Special Envoy for Iran to Muscat/Doha within 72 hours to convert the lapsed 60-day MOU window into a written 45-day technical extension whose sole deliverable is a verification protocol — IAEA re-access to the struck sites, continuous monitoring at enrichment cascades, and a freeze at current stockpile levels — with the US formally certifying in writing that it will not authorize or join strikes during the extension so long as the freeze holds.
supportingActions: Send the Vice President and National Security Advisor to the Hill to force the sanctions-relief question to an actual INARA vote rather than letting it die in ambiguity — trading a commitment to submit any comprehensive deal for congressional review in exchange for leadership shelving the new bipartisan Iran/Russia sanctions bill until the extension window closes, so Tehran is not handed proof that Washington cannot deliver.

Deliver a private, unpublicized message to the Israeli prime minister: no green light and no intelligence-sharing for unilateral action during the extension, paired with an explicit reaffirmation of the standing air-defense and munitions replenishment package and a joint contingency planning cell — abandonment insurance in exchange for restraint, with no public criticism of Israel that would harden the coalition.
decision.reasoning: I claimed credit for this MOU, so its collapse is a loss against a booked gain, and I will spend real capital to prevent it — but with Congress unratified I have no economic lever, so the only currency I have is verification-for-restraint diplomacy and alliance management. Squeezing Israel publicly risks abandonment behavior and a unilateral strike that entraps me; giving Israel a blank check invites the same outcome, so the answer is private restraint paired with visible defensive commitment. Forcing the Hill to a real vote is the only path to the deal's central economic term, and even a failed vote is more useful to me than indefinite ambiguity that Tehran reads as US incapacity.
decision.researchNote: Two-level games (Putnam) dominates: the binding constraint is not Iranian or Israeli preferences but an unratified domestic win-set, so the cycle's central move is manufacturing a credible congressional path while buying time with verification diplomacy.

entangledEffect.label: entangled escalation (dampened by active US mediation)
